key_points: Official setup flow requires installing the Computer Use plugin and granting Screen Recording + Accessibility on macOS before GUI automation tasks.
Introduces Locked Use for macOS: Codex can continue a Computer Use task after the Mac locks using a short-lived, scoped unlock flow.
Docs explicitly note background limitations: macOS can continue background tasks while Windows remains foreground-only and can’t automate Terminal or Codex itself.
May 21 2026 release notes introduced Goal mode, richer context handling, Appshots, in-app browser annotation, and locked computer use.
May 14 2026 added Codex availability in the ChatGPT mobile app for connected remote review and steering.
Signals Codex shifting from one-off tasks toward long-running workflows with cross-device continuity.
OpenAI rolled out Codex version 26.527 on May 29, 2026 for Windows GUI control via Computer Use.
Windows mode runs on active desktop, so the agent uses foreground pointer control and is best for supervised, screen-focused sessions.
Article highlights mobile steering from phone and the regional limitation of Europe exclusion for that rollout.
April 16, 2026 is framed as Codex desktop background control launch for macOS with tasks running while user keeps working.
Explains practical parallel-agent behavior with its own cursor for GUI operations.
Positions background computer use as useful for overnight automation and long-running desktop QA workflows.
Claims Codex desktop v26.415 shipped April 16 with background computer use and more than 90 plugins.
Lists heavy usage areas for plugin-led workflows in design, docs, dev, communication, and DevOps tooling.
Frames plugin install as a key competitive differentiator versus agent tools that remain mostly IDE-only or narrow-surface.

stats.fact: OpenAI states Codex now has more than 5 million weekly active users, up more than 6x since desktop app launch in February.
stats.source: OpenAI — Codex is becoming a productivity tool for everyone (June 2, 2026)

stats.fact: Knowledge workers account for about 20% of Codex users and are growing more than three times as fast as developer usage growth.
stats.source: OpenAI — Codex is becoming a productivity tool for everyone

stats.fact: Codex now supports locked computer use on macOS, allowing remote continuation after lock via a narrow authorization window and auto-lock fallback.
stats.source: OpenAI Developers docs + OpenAI Codex release notes + MacRumors coverage (May 22, 2026)

stats.fact: Computer Use on Windows launched in Codex v26.527 on May 29, 2026, described as foreground-only with remote control paths from ChatGPT mobile or macOS hosts.
stats.source: TechTimes coverage; OpenAI Help Center Codex remote access notes

stats.fact: May 21 2026 updates introduced Appshots and in-app browser annotation as workflow accelerators, supporting longer-running and multi-surface runs.
